title: Best Keywords to Target with Google Ads for Massage  - Scaling Wellness

facts.fact: The Scaling Wellness article 'Best Keywords to Target with Google Ads for Massage' was published on September 8, 2025.
Scaling Wellness defines high intent keywords as search terms showing someone is ready to take action, such as booking an appointment, making a purchase, or hiring help.
facts.quote: High intent keywords are search terms that show someone is ready to take action—like booking an appointment, making a purchase, or hiring help.

facts.fact: Scaling Wellness calls service-plus-location keywords (for example, 'deep tissue massage near me') 'bottom-of-the-funnel' terms and says Google Ads budget should focus on them first.
facts.quote: These are “bottom-of-the-funnel” keywords that’re used by people who are actively looking to book an appointment. This is where your Google Ads budget should focus first.

facts.fact: Scaling Wellness advises that broad terms such as 'massage' or 'massage therapist' without a location will attract people outside the service area or people just browsing.
facts.quote: Keywords like “massage” or “massage therapist” without a location will attract people from outside your service area, or worse, people just browsing.

facts.fact: Scaling Wellness recommends adding these negative keywords for most massage businesses: 'free', 'school', 'DIY', 'how to', 'salary', 'jobs', 'at home', and 'massage gun'.

facts.fact: Scaling Wellness says bidding on competitor business names often leads to low conversion and click fraud, unless the advertiser has a specific legal strategy or brand awareness play.
facts.quote: Unless you have a specific legal strategy or brand awareness play, bidding on competitor business names often leads to low conversion and click fraud.

facts.fact: Scaling Wellness lists Pain Relief keywords for massage ad groups as 'back pain massage', 'neck pain massage', and 'sciatica relief massage'.
facts.quote: | Pain Relief | back pain massage, neck pain massage, sciatica relief massage |

facts.fact: Scaling Wellness recommends building keyword lists from what clients say at intake, since front-desk intake forms reveal why clients booked.
facts.quote: Look through your intake forms or ask your front desk what clients say when describing why they booked. That’s your goldmine.
